raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Scope

Integrate the NPU CPU-offload allocation adaptation from #43824 and the shared Murmur uint32 correction from #43825 on the measured `release/v0.5.20` baseline, `94602c9c2b7cbdb8efd5c52802dac6a1c180089e`.

| Component | Preserved source head | Ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #43824 | `3eee99579cd3a38e95e642c1af5fba543a7f198e` | One-line shared OffloaderV1 NPU pinned-memory allocation adaptation |
| #43825 | `ebcec6e4a5416066688e6a5eb71af7476cf21ed7` | One-line shared sampling integer-semantics correction; the implementation is not NPU-only |

Both original heads remain ancestors of this integration branch. The final diff contains exactly their seven files, including the existing tests and preserved evidence. Each component's files are byte-identical to its source PR. No withdrawn compilation, attention-wrapper or kernel changes are reintroduced. The original PRs remain open drafts for component review; this PR neither closes them nor any outstanding issue.

## Validation

Fresh local checks on the integrated source: four CPU-offload allocation-policy tests passed; Python syntax checks passed for all four changed Python files; Ruff F401/F821/UP037 and `git diff --check` passed. Policy tests use recording substitutes and do not establish real device execution.

No new NPU inference or sampling-kernel run has been performed on this combined commit. Existing model scores and vector evidence remain historical results tied to their original source/configuration. Unified model accuracy and cross-repository validation are pending a fixed Omni companion and an allocated NPU test environment. Keep this PR as a draft.

## Conditions and remaining work

CPU-offload delivery retains the documented prefill/decode graphs with compilation explicitly disabled; the transfer overhead remains. Independent compilation/graph compatibility is tracked by #43958 and is not fixed here. The sampling correction does not resolve all speech/audio-text discrepancies tracked by sgl-project/sglang-omni#2738.

The original realtime companion is sgl-project/sglang-omni#2426. A consolidated Omni companion is being prepared separately. Current Omni main pins a newer SGLang/PyTorch stack, so this release-based branch must not be presented as an already-validated match for current Omni main. Upstream review, full CI and the final merge method remain pending.

@@ -9,7 +9,7 @@ def rotl32(x, r: tl.constexpr) -> tl.uint32:
     rotate left 32-bit integer x by r bits
     e.g. x = 01110001, r = 2 -> 11000101
     """
-    x = x.to(tl.uint64)
+    x = x.to(tl.uint64) & 0xFFFFFFFF
     return ((x << r) | (x >> (32 - r))) & 0xFFFFFFFF

@@ -110,7 +110,7 @@ def maybe_offload_to_cpu(self, module: torch.nn.Module) -> torch.nn.Module:
         if self._cpu_offload_bytes >= self._cpu_offload_max_bytes:
             return module
 
-        pin_memory = is_pin_memory_available()
+        pin_memory = is_pin_memory_available() or device.type == "npu"
         # offload parameters to CPU
         # use pin_memory if possible, which helps cudagraph capture speed
         offloaded_parameters = False

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+# Murmur32 high-bit regression
+
+Run `pytest test/manual/murmur_uint32/test_murmur_uint32_npu.py` in the patched SGLang release environment on an Ascend NPU. This is the existing 16-column regression. It uses deterministic integer reference values and skips without torch_npu / an NPU; a skip is not a hardware pass.
+
+`murmur_vector_results.json` is preserved evidence from a separate earlier 128-output check (8 seed/position pairs, 16 columns each). Original mismatches: 72; corrected mismatches: 0. All expected and observed integers are included. No fresh device run is claimed for packaging this evidence. No host identity, credentials, audio or model prompts are included.

@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+"""Regression vector for uint32 rotation with the most significant bit set."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+pytest.importorskip("torch_npu")
+from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling.murmur_hash import murmur_hash32
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.npu.is_available(), reason="Requires an Ascend NPU")
+def test_murmur_high_bit_columns():
+    seed = torch.tensor([2092917972], dtype=torch.uint64, device="npu")
+    position = torch.tensor([88], dtype=torch.int64, device="npu")
+    columns = torch.arange(16, device="npu")
+    # Independent 32-bit Murmur3 reference; columns 1,2,5,6,7,10,11,12,15
+    # set the high bit after the first multiply in the column mixing step.
+    expected = [
+        [
+            3847850963,
+            2821684749,
+            3379976169,
+            551063260,
+            3868596079,
+            3051706844,
+            234660108,
+            1276890786,
+            2134884091,
+            1601909887,
+            3088546729,
+            907784942,
+            2462296977,
+            2633501825,
+            3345631188,
+            2252777896,
+        ]
+    ]
+    assert murmur_hash32(seed, position, columns).cpu().tolist() == expected

@@ -0,0 +1,13 @@
+# NPU CPU-offload policy regression
+
+Run from the SGLang repository root:
+
+```bash
+python test/manual/npu_cpu_offload/test_cpu_offload_policy.py --source python/sglang/srt/utils/offloader.py
+```
+
+The four tests execute the actual OffloaderV1 class extracted from source with fake allocation boundaries. They check NPU pinning, unchanged non-NPU policy, layouts, parameter-budget behavior, zero budget and already-CPU parameters. They require no torch or accelerator, and do not test real forward execution, copies or graph capture.
+
+Historical real Qwen3-ASR-0.6B validation used SGLang 0.5.20, torch/torch_npu 2.10 and CANN 9.0. Offload 0/4 each completed 20 requests with graphs disabled, and 20 requests each with prefill/decode graphs enabled and torch.compile explicitly disabled. In the latter pair all responses matched, both scored 2/216 word edits, and loading memory was 1.63/0.78 GB. The pin-only source SHA256 is 9013301d64d73f1c1a3ac04797bd3744f15792b4d9d5d5302d2b54e7380d1f7b. Original source and failure records remain preserved locally.
+
+Do not infer torch.compile compatibility from these results. The graph-disabled YAML retained a compile setting, but graph compilation was not demonstrated in that configuration. The graph-enabled passing profile explicitly used enable_torch_compile=false. Default compile/graph problems are tracked separately from this basic offload fix.

@@ -0,0 +1,158 @@
+"""CPU-only policy regression against the actual OffloaderV1 source AST.
+
+Usage: python test_cpu_offload_policy.py --source /path/to/offloader.py
+No torch/NPU imports. Tensor allocation is a recording boundary; the real
+class controls selection, budget and parameter replacement. This does NOT
+test real pinned allocation, copies, forward, or graph correctness.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import ast
+import types
+import unittest
+
+
+class Device:
+    def __init__(self, name):
+        self.type = name
+
+    def __eq__(self, other):
+        return isinstance(other, Device) and self.type == other.type
+
+
+class Tensor:
+    dtype = "float32"
+    layout = "strided"
+
+    def __init__(self, device, size, stride, pinned=False):
+        self.device = Device(device)
+        self._size = size
+        self._stride = stride
+        self.pinned = pinned
+        self.copied_from = None
+
+    def size(self):
+        return self._size
+
+    def stride(self):
+        return self._stride
+
+    def numel(self):
+        result = 1
+        for n in self._size:
+            result *= n
+        return result
+
+    def element_size(self):
+        return 4
+
+    def copy_(self, source):
+        self.copied_from = source
+
+
+class Parameter:
+    def __init__(self, data):
+        self.data = data
+
+    @property
+    def device(self):
+        return self.data.device
+
+
+class Module:
+    def __init__(self, device):
+        self.items = [
+            Parameter(Tensor(device, (2, 3), (1, 2))),
+            Parameter(Tensor(device, (2, 3), (3, 1))),
+        ]
+        self.forward = lambda *a, **k: None
+
+    def parameters(self):
+        return iter(self.items)
+
+
+def load_class(source, platform_pin):
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    cls = next(
+        n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "OffloaderV1"
+    )
+    allocations = []
+
+    def allocate(**kw):
+        allocations.append(kw)
+        return Tensor(kw["device"], kw["size"], kw["stride"], kw["pin_memory"])
+
+    namespace = {
+        "BaseOffloader": object,
+        "torch": types.SimpleNamespace(device=Device, empty_strided=allocate),
+        "is_pin_memory_available": lambda: platform_pin,
+    }
+    # Keep class/function code exactly from --source; postpone annotations only.
+    unit = ast.Module(
+        body=[
+            ast.ImportFrom(
+                module="__future__", names=[ast.alias(name="annotations")], level=0
+            ),
+            cls,
+        ],
+        type_ignores=[],
+    )
+    exec(
+        compile(ast.fix_missing_locations(unit), "<actual OffloaderV1>", "exec"),
+        namespace,
+    )
+    return namespace["OffloaderV1"], allocations
+
+
+class PolicyTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    source = ""
+
+    def test_npu_pins_offloaded_storage_without_changing_layout(self):
+        cls, allocations = load_class(self.source, False)
+        module = Module("npu")
+        original = module.items[0].data
+        cls(24).maybe_offload_to_cpu(module)
+        self.assertTrue(allocations[0]["pin_memory"])
+        self.assertEqual(module.items[0].data.stride(), original.stride())
+        self.assertIs(module.items[0].data.copied_from, original)
+
+    def test_non_npu_preserves_platform_policy(self):
+        for target in ("cuda", "xpu"):
+            for available in (False, True):
+                with self.subTest(target=target, available=available):
+                    cls, allocations = load_class(self.source, available)
+                    cls(24).maybe_offload_to_cpu(Module(target))
+                    self.assertEqual(allocations[0]["pin_memory"], available)
+
+    def test_budget_counts_existing_parameter_granularity_across_modules(self):
+        cls, allocations = load_class(self.source, False)
+        offloader = cls(25)  # Existing contract: whole parameter may cross cap.
+        first, second = Module("npu"), Module("npu")
+        offloader.maybe_offload_to_cpu(first)
+        offloader.maybe_offload_to_cpu(second)
+        self.assertEqual(len(allocations), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(offloader._cpu_offload_bytes, 48)
+        self.assertEqual([p.device.type for p in second.items], ["npu", "npu"])
+
+    def test_zero_budget_and_cpu_module_leave_storage_untouched(self):
+        for target, budget in (("npu", 0), ("cpu", 100)):
+            cls, allocations = load_class(self.source, False)
+            module = Module(target)
+            old = [p.data for p in module.items]
+            offloader = cls(budget)
+            offloader.maybe_offload_to_cpu(module)
+            self.assertEqual(allocations, [])
+            self.assertEqual(offloader._cpu_offload_bytes, 0)
+            self.assertEqual([p.data for p in module.items], old)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    from pathlib import Path
+
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--source", required=True, type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    PolicyTests.source = args.source.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    suite = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(PolicyTests)
+    result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(suite)
+    raise SystemExit(not result.wasSuccessful())
